title: Product of probability laws
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets, and let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability mass functions on $A$ and $B$, respectively. Define their product law on $A\times B$ by first drawing $a$ according to $\mu$, then drawing $b$ according to $\nu$, independently of $a$, and returning $(a,b)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ is a probability mass function on $A$
$\nu$ is a probability mass function on $B$
